Subject: Recap + next steps — streaming latency & SLA language

Hi Jake — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the SOW/SLA aligned with your procurement team:

Summary of what we discussed (please correct if I got anything wrong):
- Target latency goals: p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming generative calls, streaming first-byte p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 800ms for live transcript scenarios.
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 500 concurrent streaming sessions per region, burstable to 1,500 for scheduled events (1–2 hour windows).
- Measurement window: monthly SLO, measured daily and aggregated monthly with rolling 30-day lookback.
- Exclusions you asked about: network-level client interrupts, deliberate client cancellations, and multi-region failover periods — we should define thresholds.
- Reporting: weekly health snapshot to your CS contact + formal monthly SLO report (dashboard link + CSV).
- Remedies: service credit ladder tied to monthly SLO breaches (we'll propose wording).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a first-pass SLA language and measurement definitions (attached).
2) Aditya (cc) — can you confirm how Redwood measures streaming latencies (start/end points, p95/p99 definitions, and what we recommend excluding)?
3) Jake — if procurement wants different measurement windows or a different remedies ladder, please flag now so we can iterate.

Attachments: redwood_sla_draft_v1.docx (draft language), latency-measurement-diagram.png (visual for how we define start/end).

Thanks — aim to get a redline from you by Wed so we can move to legal/procurement.

— Olga

Thanks Olga — quick clarifications from our side after regrouping with infra: 

- Streaming measurement: we care most about first-byte latency for live UX (p95), but we also want a sense of session completion latency for post-call processing (p99). Is it feasible to provide both?
- Exclusions: we definitely want client-driven cancels excluded. The tricky one is intermittent network blips in the hospital network; we need a clear definition so procurement can sign off (they prefer numeric thresholds vs free text).
- Remedies: procurement will want the credit ladder spelled out and an option to escalate to an SLA review call if we see repeated breaches (3+ months).

We'll review your draft; please put the measurement thresholds and exclusion numeric cutoffs in the draft so procurement can evaluate.

Subject: RE: Recap + next steps — streaming latency & SLA language

Jake — thanks for the specifics. Level-setting from engineering/measurement: below is how Redwood currently measures streaming latency and some recommended exclusion thresholds you can feed to procurement. I'll also propose short SLA wording that maps to our reporting / remedy system.

Measurement definitions (streaming):
- "Streaming first-byte latency": measured from server-side receipt of the first valid client request byte (TCP/TLS application layer) to the time the first token byte is emitted by the model runtime and forwarded to the client (server-side send).
- "Streaming completion latency": time from request receipt to final token emitted and flush completed (useful for post-call processing).
- Percentiles: we report p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and completion latency per 1-minute aggregation buckets, then aggregate to hourly/daily/monthly windows.

Exclusions (recommended numeric rules):
1) Client-initiated cancel/stop: exclude if server logs show explicit cancel within 2s of start.
2) Network disconnects: exclude if TCP/TLS session resets or client RST before 500ms of server send — otherwise counted.
3) Keepalives/idle drop: streams idle > 15 minutes are considered aborted and excluded from SLO (we count active sessions only).
4) Multi-region failover: exclude window if customer signals a planned region migration and we schedule traffic cutover (must be logged in our incident system).

Reporting cadence and evidence:
- Weekly snapshot (automated): p95/p99 for first-byte and completion, average concurrency, top 10 time-of-day percentiles.
- Monthly formal report: CSV of per-minute aggregates, incident log with root cause and mitigation, and a one-page summary.

SLA/remedies (proposal):
- If monthly p95(first-byte) > target, service credit = 5% of monthly invoice.
- If monthly p99(first-byte) > target, additional 7% credit.
- Cap: cumulative credits per month capped at 30% of monthly invoice.
- Repeated breaches (3 of 6 consecutive months): option for an SLA review meeting and contract remediation (including escalation to engineering leadership).

Notes on measurement fairness: we anchor measurement at server receipt (not client-side time) to avoid clock skews and client-side variability. For streaming specifically, first-byte is the most actionable for UX.

Laura/Soojin — two asks: 1) can we surface the per-minute CSV in the shared Drive link and 2) do we want to add a postmortem delivery SLA for incidents > 4 hours?

— Aditya

Jake — this wording looks good from CS/ops. Two small edits we recommend for procurement readability:

1) Replace the phrase "exclude if client RST" with "exclude if client-initiated TCP reset is recorded within 500ms of server send" (explicit)
2) Add a reporting cadence bullet: "SLA review cadence: on-breach immediate notification + 3 business-day preliminary incident summary; full postmortem within 10 business days for incidents > 4 hours."

We will upload the per-minute CSV and an example dashboard CSV to the Drive link (sharing ACL: NovaHealth-read). Also attached: redwood_sla_draft_v1.docx (with Aditya's numeric thresholds incorporated) and latency-measurement-diagram.png.
